meta.title: SteamGiftBot — SteamGifts & IndieGala giveaway bot
meta.description: Open-source bot that auto-enters SteamGifts, IndieGala and OpiumPulses giveaways and claims free games on Steam, GOG and itch.io. Web panel and Telegram.
meta.ogAlt: SteamGiftBot: a giveaway bot for SteamGifts, IndieGala, OpiumPulses, Steam, GOG and itch.io

hero.desc: Enters giveaways on SteamGifts, IndieGala and OpiumPulses, claims free games on Steam, GOG and itch.io, and messages you on Telegram when you win.

facts.sites: three with giveaways for site currency, three with free games
facts.pw: the farm signs in with your browser's cookies and never sees a password

farm.title: A panel, not a terminal.
farm.lead: Each site runs in its own thread, and the panel shows which one is busy, why another is waiting and what went out over the last day.
farm.open: Open the screenshot at full size
farm.hint: Click a screenshot to open it at full size.
farm.s1: Wins, entries per day and why each site is waiting. You don't have to read the log to see what is going on.
farm.s1alt: The farm's overview: new wins, a chart of entries per day and the state of each site
farm.s2: Every giveaway on offer and the decision for each: enter, or why it is skipped. Not a single point spent.
farm.s2alt: IndieGala dry run: two giveaways it would enter, two skipped with a reason
farm.s3: Copy the site's request as cURL and paste it. The farm checks the sign in without saving anything and shows the balance.
farm.s3alt: Connect wizard for GOG: numbered steps and a box for the request
farm.s4: Working hours, daily limits, no DLC or adult games, nothing you already own. Your wishlist goes first.
farm.s4alt: Farm settings: time zone, sites that start on boot, Telegram, Steam library and ArchiSteamFarm
farm.s5: The same panel with tabs at the bottom of the screen. Add it to your home screen and it opens like an app.
farm.s5alt: The farm's overview on a phone: wins, counters and the bottom tab bar
farm.c1: Wins, expired cookies and a daily summary. Commands: /status, /pause, /run, /preview.
farm.c2: A won key is activated on Steam with one button; free Steam games land in your library on their own.
farm.c3: Any computer that stays on. The panel is visible only on your network or through Tailscale.

sites.title: Six sites.
sites.lead: Three sites with giveaways for their own currency and three sources of free games. Each row opens its wiki page.
sites.st: games Steam gives away to keep
sites.free: The command line bot also tells you about free games on Epic, GOG and other stores, using GamerPower's list.

odds.title: Where the odds are.
odds.lead: On IndieGala the farm puts first the giveaways with the best chance per Galasilver spent: 1 / ((entrants + 1) × price). Move the sliders.

install.title: Install.
install.lead: The farm is for a computer that stays on: on Windows it is one download, elsewhere it runs from source. The command line bot is for SteamGifts alone.
install.farm1: Get the code and its dependencies. Needs Python 3.10 or newer.
install.farm2: Set the panel's password and start the farm on your computer's LAN address.
install.farm3: Open http://192.168.1.10:8092, sign in and connect a site. A systemd service, the firewall and phones are covered in the README.
install.farmNote: On Windows there is nothing to install: BotFarm.exe is on the Windows tab.
install.exe1: Download BotFarm.exe (the farm with its panel) or SteamGiftBot.exe (SteamGifts alone), with its .sha256, from releases, into a folder of its own. No Python needed.
install.exe2: Check the checksum against the line in the .sha256 file.
install.exe3: Run it. BotFarm.exe asks once for a password for its panel and opens the panel in your browser; SteamGiftBot.exe asks for the cookie and a few settings.
install.docker1: Put the SteamGifts cookie (the PHPSESSID value) in a secret file, so that docker inspect does not show it.
install.docker2: Start the container. It does not run as root; the image is built for amd64 and arm64.
install.dockerNote: This is the command line bot, SteamGifts only. The same image runs the farm with -m steamgiftbot.farm --data; see the README.

faq.title: FAQ.
faq.lead: The short version. The rest is in the README and the wiki.
faq.a1: It can. SteamGifts forbids auto-entry scripts, and other sites have rules of their own. The farm pauses, backs off when a site asks, and never works around Cloudflare or captchas, but the decision and the risk are yours.
faq.q2: Does the farm know my passwords?
faq.a2: No. It signs in with cookies copied from your browser and keeps them on your own computer. The panel never hands them back, not even to you.
faq.a3: Any computer that stays on will do: a mini PC, an old laptop, a Raspberry Pi. The farm spends most of its time waiting.
faq.q4: Does the panel work on a phone?
faq.a4: Yes. At home through your computer's LAN address, away through Tailscale. It can be added to the home screen.
faq.q5: Why does the farm enter nothing?
faq.a5: Open the site's dry run: every giveaway has its reason there. Most often the balance ran out or the account level is set wrong.
faq.q6: Is this an official SteamGifts project?
faq.a6: No. SteamGiftBot is an independent open source project under MPL-2.0, not affiliated with SteamGifts, IndieGala, GOG, itch.io or Valve.
faq.q7: How is the farm different from extensions like AutoJoin?
faq.a7: An extension enters giveaways while your browser is open, and only on SteamGifts. The farm runs on a server around the clock, handles six sites at once, skips games already in your Steam library and tells you about wins on Telegram.
faq.a8: Nothing. The code is open under MPL-2.0, with no subscriptions or paid features. All you need is a computer that stays on.

support.title: Free. For good.
support.lead: SteamGiftBot is built by one person in their spare time. If the farm has already brought you a game or two, you can buy the author a coffee: it pays for new sites, and for fixing old ones when they change their pages.
support.note: Support is voluntary: the farm hides no features behind a payment and shows no ads.
